title: Product square coordinates and square difference
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and let $X_i\to S$ for $i=1,2,3$ be schemes over $S$. Using fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product], put $C=(X_1\times_S X_2)\times_S X_3$, $P=(X_1\times_S X_1)\times_S(X_2\times_S X_2)$ and $Q=P\times_S X_3$. For $a,b\in\{0,1\}$, define $r_{ab}:Q\to C$ by the fibre-product universal property from the coordinate projections, so that $r_{ab}(x_0,x_1,y_0,y_1,z)=(x_a,y_b,z)$. Define $\pi:Q\to P$ to be the first projection. For an invertible $\mathcal O_C$-module $A$ [def-sc-invertible-module], its square difference is the $\mathcal O_Q$-module $$D(A)=r_{00}^*A\otimes r_{11}^*A\otimes(r_{01}^*A)^\vee\otimes(r_{10}^*A)^\vee,$$ where each pullback is the tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback], each tensor is the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and $M^\vee=\mathcal{H}om_{\mathcal O_Q}(M,\mathcal O_Q)$ is the dual of an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module]. The tensor product is associated to the right, $D(A)=r_{00}^*A\otimes(r_{11}^*A\otimes((r_{01}^*A)^\vee\otimes(r_{10}^*A)^\vee))$. These constructions require no smoothness, separatedness, finiteness or integrality hypothesis on the schemes.

source.place: Guo, Section 5.1, Theorems of cube and square: definitions of W, r_J, pi and s(L; X_1, X_2), printed p.11, March 31, 2026 version; coordinates reordered from W x_S W to (X_1 x_S X_1) x_S (X_2 x_S X_2).
